result.summary: A residential street with continuous sidewalks on both sides, separated from the roadway by a grass planting strip. The environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings and features significant pavement degradation in the center of the roadway.

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: A large area of cracked and patched asphalt in the center of the roadway may cause drivers to swerve unexpectedly.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and center of the roadway

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Crossings
hazards.description: Multiple curb cuts for residential driveways create conflict points between pedestrians and vehicles entering/exiting properties.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the sidewalk

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the degraded pavement to ensure predictable vehicle paths and improve overall safety.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install traffic calming measures to maintain low vehicle speeds appropriate for a residential street.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street with a paved sidewalk separated from the roadway by a grass buffer. The environment is generally well-maintained with clear separation between pedestrians and vehicles, though it lacks specific traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Proximity
hazards.description: A utility pole is located in the grass buffer immediately adjacent to the sidewalk edge.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground, next to the sidewalk.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees in the grass buffer would provide shade and create a stronger sense of enclosure to naturally slow traffic.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implementing speed humps or cushions would help maintain low vehicle speeds appropriate for a residential street.

result.summary: The image shows a typical residential street with sidewalks on both sides, separated from the roadway by a grass buffer. However, the environment lacks marked crossings and traffic calming, and the narrow sidewalks are obstructed by utility poles.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parking on both sides of the street obscures the visibility of pedestrians, particularly shorter individuals or children, to oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible street

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is located within the narrow sidewalk path, significantly reducing the clear width for pedestrians and creating a barrier for those with mobility devices.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, on the sidewalk

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Implement high-visibility continental crosswalk markings to clearly designate pedestrian crossing areas.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Install speed humps to physically enforce low vehicle speeds in this residential context.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a residential area with a sidewalk that terminates into a wide, unmarked paved area used for vehicle access and parking. While the low-speed residential context is beneficial, the lack of formal crossing infrastructure and sidewalk continuity creates a disorganized space for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross a large expanse of asphalt with no designated path or markings to alert drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground and midground where the sidewalk ends at the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The transition from the sidewalk to the roadway lacks a sloped ramp, creating a barrier for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: End of the sidewalk on the left side of the image

hazards.name: Sidewalk Discontinuity
hazards.description: The formal sidewalk ends abruptly, forcing pedestrians to walk in the shared vehicle space.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image where the concrete path meets the asphalt

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks to define a clear path for pedestrians and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install curb ramps at all transition points between the sidewalk and the roadway.
